facts:

White balance: near-neutral areas (18% of the frame) look neutral, about 6400 K.
Saturation: low (muted).
Skin-tone colours (faces, or any warm surface): 5% of the frame, on the skin line.
q: it's an evening scene, should it be brighter than this?
a: Mids sit about 1.8 stops below middle grey with 6% crushed blacks. For an evening scene a dark picture can be right: not every shot should reach both ends. If faces or important detail are lost, lift exposure a little on the balance node (Offset or Gain) and raise Lift so the crushed shadows keep some detail; otherwise leave it dark.

facts:
Exposure: mids about 0.6 stops above middle grey; 14% clipped highlights, 0% crushed blacks; contrast 6.2 stops (5–95 %).
White balance: near-neutral areas (12% of the frame) look neutral, about 6600 K.
Saturation: moderate.
Skin-tone colours: little or none in the frame.
a: 14% of the frame is clipped highlights. Clipped areas hold no detail to recover, so leave them white; what you can do is roll the highlights off: Highlight soft clip on a late node (Curves tab, Highlight roll-off and Roll-off knee) or a shoulder on the master curve, so the edge into white is soft. Too much makes whites grey.

q: it's a foggy morning shot, how much contrast should I add?
a: Contrast is only about 2.1 stops (5–95 %) and saturation low, which is what fog looks like. Not every shot should reach both ends of the waveform: add a little Contrast with the Pivot at the subject's brightness (`grade.param.contrast`, `grade.param.pivot`) so the subject stays put, and stop while it still reads as fog.

q: my beach shot looks blown out
a: Mids are about 1.4 stops above middle grey and 22% of the frame is clipped: overexposed. Bring Gain / Offset down on the balance node to set the brightest detail just under the top of the waveform; what is clipped stays white, so roll it off with Highlight soft clip rather than pulling it grey.
